label: copy phase from 3rd output on, input-token-selective (j, r, l, g, o, n, i, v, x, h)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, from recall_idx 2 onward (never in the original phase, at <DEL>, or on the first two outputs; never on the first occurrence of a token). Within that window it is selective for the fed-back input token: j strongly (25% rate, 23% of mass), then r, l, g, o, n, i, v, x, h; digits are weak. Activity is higher on the last two outputs (to_go <= 1) and in short sequences (L=3,4); the top activations are the final step of L=3 sequences with j as the second token (e.g. w j t <DEL> w [j]). The copy-window gate alone has ~100% recall but 14% precision; the token restriction gives dev F1 0.46 / mass recall 0.80. Firing on a given step is context-dependent, and the predicate does not capture it fully.
